status_meanings.disputed: sources disagree; both are listed in the record's notes
status_meanings.unverifiable: the fact appears only in secondary sources; no primary source could be obtained
status_meanings.verified: the value in the wiki matches the primary source

records.fact: Building blocks — no branch prediction unit; simple 4-bit CPU with fixed instruction cycle
records.previous_value: Fetch + branch prediction listed among its building blocks
records.current_value: Complete 4-bit parallel CPU; 1-word instructions are 8 bits requiring 8 clock periods (one instruction cycle), 2-word instructions 16 clock periods; no branch prediction block in the datasheet architecture

source.title: 4004 Single Chip 4-Bit P-Channel Microprocessor (Intel 4004 datasheet)
source.locator: Page 8-15, description paragraph; Instruction Set Format section, page 8-17

records.quote: The Intel® 4004 is a complete 4-bit parallel central processing unit (CPU).
records.notes: Absence of branch prediction cannot be proved by a single positive sentence; the correction rests on the datasheet's complete architectural description, which lists the accumulator, index registers, pointer stack, instruction encoding/decoder, timing and control — with no prediction or speculative-fetch mechanism — and defines the fixed cycle in the Instruction Set Format section: a 1-word instruction is 8 bits requiring 8 clock periods (instruction cycle) and a 2-word instruction is 16 bits requiring 16 clock periods (2 instruction cycles). Conditional branching exists (JCN), but it is resolved in the normal instruction cycle, not predicted. Datasheet text is via Intel's original document archived at archive.org; OCR in the archived copy is imperfect outside the quoted sentence.
